Metabolic rewiring in the brain microenvironment

The brain interstitial space and the cerebrospinal fluid are poor in glucose. Thus, metastatic cells upregulate the enzymes to catabolize glucose efficiently and make use of alternative metabolites including branched-chain amino acids (BCAA), acetate, glutamine (also contributing to antioxidant defense through the antiport with cysteine), γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) and speculatively ketone bodies. Furthermore, metastatic cells upregulate de novo synthesis pathways to feed membrane and nucleotide synthesis necessary for proliferation. However, resident cells metabolically support cancer cells by supplying nutrients such as glucose, fatty acids, speculatively through gap junctions, and enhance protumorous signaling via glutamate-activated N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR). FBP2, Fructose bisphosphatase 2; PCK1/2, Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase 1/2; LDH, Lactate dehydrogenase, NK, Natural killer; ACSS2, Acyl-coenzyme A synthetase short-chain family member 2; PHGDH, Phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase; SREBP1, Sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1; FASN, Fatty acid synthase; ACC1, Acetyl-CoA carboxylase 1; TCA, Tricarboxylic acid; ETC, Electron transport chain; ATP, Adenosine triphosphate; α-KG, α-Ketoglutarate; SLC7A11, Solute carrier family 7 member 11; ROS, Reactive oxygen species; PPARγ, Peroxisome proliferator activated receptor gamma; miR-122, microRNA 122
